title: Tom Brown's brother and the origin of slap bass
summary: He remembers Tom Brown's brother, with Goldkette, as credited with starting slap bass, and owns one Rhythm Kings record.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah. Did you remember many other people playing that style here, of slapping the bass?

No. I remember hearing Tom Brown's brother. He was with Gene Goldcat. But I didn't know who he was at the time. I only had the pleasure of meeting him within the last few years, when I became associated with Tom Brown through the New Orleans Jazz Club. And not many years before Tom passed away, his brother visited here, and then I was able to meet him. Yeah. He played that same style. He played that style. And he was given credit, I think, for being a man that started that. Yes. In fact, I read that in a publication of the International Musicians.
I remember Tom showed us that article.
Yeah. I think they made some award to his brother. Yeah. In recognition of his starting that slapping on the bass.
But you never heard him in person in the old days down here?

That's right. But not too much, though, because I remember it was here. I think he was with the Rhythm Kings. Is that correct? In Chicago? He played here before. And I have only one of their records, I think. And maybe I should have more. But I have She's Crying For Me Blues. And on the other side, I think, is Maple Leaf Strut. Is that right? Or Maple Leaf Rag. Oh, Golden Leaf. Golden Leaf Strut. That's right. Mm-hmm.
